key_insight: eMOOD replaces MOOD’s classical troubled-cell test with an entropy-based detector, enabling more targeted shock capture while keeping high-order accuracy on unstructured meshes.
engineering_relevance: The method can reduce unnecessary fallback reconstructions and memory traffic in large-scale compressible-flow solvers, improving efficiency for multiphase and shock-dominated simulations.
method: Computes numerical entropy production as a compact troubled-cell indicator.
Integrates the detector into both standard MOOD cascades and a MOOD-CWENO hybrid.
Uses the open-source UCNS3D solver for high-order finite-volume simulations on unstructured meshes.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark problems including Shu-Osher, double Mach reflection, forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble interaction, and triple material point cases, eMOOD flags up to 75% fewer cells and achieves up to 20% speed-up while preserving solution quality.
watch_item: Entropy-based detection must remain robust across very different flow regimes, since overly aggressive or mislocalized flagging could still degrade accuracy or efficiency in strongly heterogeneous multiphase cases.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
